text.p: Martin Marietta Materials Inc said Wednesday it has acquired rights to commercialize two technologies related to the materials business.

The company said it acquired rights to composites technology developed by Lockheed Martin Corp for applications other than sales to the U.S. Department of Defense. The composites produce products where corrosion resistance and strength-to-weight ratios are important.
This material can potentially be used in such applications as bridge decks and structures, rail and tank cars, drilling platforms and other marine structures, Martin Marietta said.
The company said it hired a Manager of Composites to pursue commercialization and expects to put at least two composite bridges into service in 1997 for field evaluation.

The company also is negotiating an agreement which could introduce this technology into the international market in the near future, it said. Initial production of composite products is being handled by outside toll manufacturers.

Martin Marietta Materials said it has also acquired the U.S. rights to a patented microwave technology for use in cleaning the inside of mixer drums on ready-mixed concrete trucks. Currently, this task is performed manually with jackhammers.
The company expects to conduct extensive field testing during the first half of 1997 and to begin marketing this service in the second half of 1997.
Martin Marietta Materials said it holds an option on the technology for use in international markets and will be evaluating this potential over the next 60 days.
